name: 1MP x4 OV9782 color global-shutter quad kit (Camarray HAT)
stereo_sync: four sensors on a Camarray HAT, synced in hardware
driver: Arducam; the Jetson ISP is not supported (raw)

name: 1MP OV9782 color global-shutter USB camera (UVC, M12 low-distortion lens)
trigger_notes: pins F (trigger) and G (GND); rising edge, >= 2 us high; up to 90 fps in MJPG; Linux: v4l2-ctl -c exposure_dynamic_framerate=1
notes: MJPEG only at speed: JPEG artefacts on the ball's edge and a decode on the host, latency unmeasured. USB 2.0 inferred from YUY2 at 10 fps (est). Price VERIFY.

name: 1MP OV9281 mono global-shutter camera for Raspberry Pi
trigger_notes: XVS on UC-788 boards; B0165 Rev B lacks trigger_mode
driver: upstream ov9281 driver in the Raspberry Pi kernel; Arducam per-L4T on Jetson
notes: Mono: the robot's colour-blob detector would need a shape / motion detector instead. Full-resolution 120 fps is the sensor's (est).

name: 1MP x2 OV9281 mono global-shutter stereo kit
notes: Mono. Price is the OV9281 stereo bundle's listing (SKU match VERIFY).

name: 5MP OG05B10 color global-shutter camera for Raspberry Pi
notes: Too slow at full resolution for the catch (30 fps); cropped modes VERIFY.

name: AR0234 Full HD color global-shutter camera for Jetson Orin NX / Orin Nano
trigger_notes: 3.3 V on CN3 pin 2 (e.g. from header pin 15 as PWM); GMSL variants take 1.8 V only
stereo_sync: one trigger line to both cameras (e-con: 'synchronization between two cameras can be achieved')
notes: The only Jetson camera found with a vendor-documented hardware trigger on Orin Nano / NX. Price on request. The Teensy's CAM_TRIG is 3.3 V: matches (no 1.8 V shifter).

name: Raspberry Pi Global Shutter Camera (IMX296)
trigger_notes: XTR, 1.8 V (3.3 V can damage it); exposure = low pulse + 14.26 us; frame rate = trigger rate; remove R11 if Q2 is fitted; imx296 trigger_mode module parameter
stereo_sync: one XTR line to both (or the XMASTER solder link)
driver: upstream imx296 in the Raspberry Pi kernel
availability: Mouser $50 (152 in stock, VERIFY); PiShop $55 and SparkFun $63.75 stock unclear / backorder; Adafruit $50 and Micro Center out of stock (2026-10-28)
notes: 60 fps at full resolution (higher with cropping: VERIFY). No lens: Arducam LN051 3.2 mm CS ($29.99) gives ~76 x 60 deg if rectilinear (est; the sim assumes 70 deg vertical; it is sold as 120 deg on the larger HQ sensor, so expect barrel distortion: VERIFY). A Pi 5 cable is in the box since Aug 2025 (Adafruit). C/CS lenses are large: an M12 IMX296 board (Arducam $110, Waveshare $66-83) is the compact form, trigger pin VERIFY. Latency on a Pi 5 unpublished: measure trigger to detection.

name: OAK-FFC 4P (RVC2) camera board
trigger_notes: FSIN on the board's connector, 1.8 V; FSIN_4LANE / FSIN_2LANE joined with MXIO6; GPIO38 high on R6+
driver: DepthAI (Linux, Windows, macOS; x86 and ARM)
latency_notes: mono 800p at 120 fps, frame stamp to host, USB 3.2 Gen 1 (color through its ISP: 33 ms at 1080p60)
notes: Two 4-lane + two 2-lane camera ports; ISP, stereo depth and small networks on board; BNO086 IMU; 5 V barrel. Units after May 2026 have no eMMC. Makes the camera pair host-agnostic (any USB 3 computer).

name: OAK-FFC OV9782 module
notes: The design's sensor (design.md: OV9782 at 120 fps, MCU-triggered). Lens and FOV options VERIFY.

name: RealSense D435
sensor: IR pair + depth: 2 x global-shutter mono imagers (OmniVision OV9282, VERIFY); RGB: rolling shutter (OV2740, VERIFY)
connector: USB 3.0 Type-C; 9-pin JST SH sync connector on the back
trigger_notes: inter_cam_sync_mode 0..4 is offered by firmware 5.17.3.10; that a slave mode follows an external 1.8 V pulse is VERIFY
driver: librealsense 2.59.1: Windows (metadata needs a registry change); Linux aarch64 pip wheel on V4L (works on a Pi 4, metadata out of the box)
availability: in hand (owned, Fernando's bench; on omni-cam)
prov_overrides: reseller: shutter, res_w_px, res_h_px; est: sensor, pixel_um, fps_full; measured: baseline_mm, fps_modes, driver
notes: Fernando's unit: serial 827312072573, firmware 5.17.3.10 (updated from 5.9.2). The IR pair is mono: the colour-blob detector needs colour, and the RGB camera is rolling shutter, so it is a reference for the sensor family and a depth source, not the catch camera. On the PC it links only at USB 2.1 (three cables, three ports); on a Pi 4's blue port it links at USB 3.2 and every mode runs. No price entered (owned). Sensor models, pixel size and the 30 fps at 1280x800 are VERIFY.
meas_notes: IR pair 848x480@90, 1 ms fixed exposure, on a Pi 4 over USB 3.2: mid-exposure to pixels in numpy, median 10.3 ms (p95 10.3), 0 lost of 5393 in 60 s with depth; auto exposure (9.9 ms) 14.8 ms. NOT glass to software, and without detection or transport. Calibration drift not measured. results/omni-cam/ (S207)

name: 12MP IMX708 Camera Module 3 (Raspberry Pi, autofocus)
trigger_notes: no trigger input used or exposed on the Pi; VERIFY
driver: imx708 kernel driver (dtoverlay=imx708); Ubuntu's libcamera 0.2 can't drive it: Raspberry Pi's libcamera fork built from source
availability: in hand (owned, Fernando's bench; on omni-cam)
notes: The Pi 4 camera-head rehearsal's camera (characterization/pi_camera). Rolling shutter is from the sensor family, not stated on the Raspberry Pi page (est). The Pi 4 is not in the platform list, so hosts says raspberry_pi_5 (the same module and driver). Arducam lists the autofocus 75 deg at USD 25 and the wide at USD 35 (S210); the owned variant and its price are not recorded, so no price is entered. Full-resolution frame rate, lanes and connector are blank, not looked up.
meas_notes: Pi 4, performance governor, 1536x864 sensor mode scaled to 768x432 at 120 fps, FastDetector on: 0 dropped of 1202; sensor-to-detection median 16.8 ms (p95 19.6). SensorTimestamp = start of readout, so the 7.9 ms exposure and the transport are not in it. pi_camera README.md (S209)
